sections.label: Executive Summary / Letter of Inquiry
sections.text:
Measure requests general operating support from the Shield-Ayres Foundation for its community-led data and evaluation work in Travis County.[^1] Measure's mission, in its own words, is to mobilise "communities to transform lived experience into data, data into power, and power into systemic change."[^2]

One matter belongs at the top of this letter rather than buried in it. The Foundation states on its own page that it "has paused its open application process" and that "Only organizations that have previously received funding from the Shield-Ayres Foundation are eligible to submit a Letter of Inquiry (LOI)."[^1] [EVIDENCE: a 990-PF Part XV record shows a grant to a recipient whose normalised name matches this organisation, in Texas, but Part XV carries no recipient EIN so the record cannot identify the recipient conclusively] [CONFIRM: whether Measure is on the Foundation's own list of prior grantees, which only the Foundation can settle]

If that gate is not met, this letter should not be sent, and no amount of drafting changes that.

sections.label: Statement of Need
sections.text:
Community organisations in Travis County are asked for evidence of impact by nearly every funder, and are rarely resourced to produce it.[^3] The result is a measurement gap that falls hardest on the smallest organisations, which are closest to the communities being described and least able to afford an evaluator.[^3]

[MISSING: current Travis County figures on nonprofit evaluation capacity, which would need to be sourced or produced rather than asserted]

sections.label: Project Description
sections.text:
Measure operates a set of programmes that together move an organisation from question to evidence to action: Data Support, which turns community questions into evidence; the CARE Model, a twelve-step community-led evaluation framework; Community Data Gatherings; Measure Ignite, a network of data-driven changemakers; and Financially Lit and Funding Ready, a six-week funding-readiness series.[^2]

Two newer initiatives extend the same method into emerging technology: Communities in the Loop, on AI literacy and civic technology, and Measure LIT, a set of micro AI-literacy trainings.[^2]

[CONFIRM: which of these programmes this request would fund, and at what scale]

sections.label: Goals, Outcomes and Evaluation
sections.text:
Measure would apply its own CARE Model to this grant, which is the same framework it asks partner organisations to use.[^2] An organisation that sells evaluation and does not evaluate itself is not credible, and the Foundation is entitled to hold this request to the standard the applicant sets for others.

[MISSING: the specific outcome targets and measurement points for the grant period, which must be set with the Foundation rather than assumed]

sections.label: Organizational Capacity
sections.text:
Measure filed total revenue of $1,254,853 and total expenses of $1,009,252 for tax year 2023, with $724,157 of that spent on programme services.[^4] That is a programme expense ratio of 71.8 per cent, computed from those two filed figures rather than reported on the form.[^4]

The organisation has grown across the filed period: revenue was $325,374 in 2021 and $745,052 in 2022 before the 2023 figure above.[^4] Net assets at the end of 2023 stood at $392,727, against $147,126 at the start of that year.[^4]

[CONFIRM: the current number of organisations supported and the cumulative value of CARE Model grants distributed. Two different figures are published for each, four weeks apart, and a cumulative total cannot decrease, so the authoritative numbers must come from Measure.]

sections.label: Alignment with Funder Priorities
sections.text:
The Foundation funds organisations whose programmes serve the communities of Bexar and Travis counties.[^1] Measure is based in Austin, in Travis County, so the geographic test is met on its face.[^2]

Two of the Foundation's stated procedural limits should be planned around rather than discovered late: an organisation may apply once in any twelve-month period, and may receive grants for up to three consecutive years.[^1] Letters of Inquiry are considered at the first and third quarterly board meetings, with deadlines of 15 February and 15 August.[^1]
